newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NZ SET ENGLAND CHALLENGING 305 TO WIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ SET ENGLAND CHALLENGING 305 TO WIN.

text.p: The England-New Zealand third test and series was set for a thrilling climax with New Zealand all out for 186 on the stroke of lunch on the fourth day on Monday, setting England 305 to win.
England already lead the three-match series 1-0.
New Zealand, who resumed their second innings at a precarious 95 for six, achieved a respectable total thanks to Chris Cairns and 18 year-old Daniel Vettori.
England have five sessions in which to score the runs, but only once in their test history have an English team scored more than 300 to win a test -- against Australia in Melbourne in 1928-29.
New Zealand need to win the test to square the three-match series after losing the second test in Wellington by an innings and 68 runs last week.
After losing the injured Matt Horne for 13 early in the day, Cairns and Vettori combined in an excellent 71-run stand off 116 balls for the eighth wicket.
Cairns went on to complete his second half century of the match, reaching 52, before being caught on the extra cover boundary off left-arm spinner Phil Tufnell.
He batted 133 minutes, faced 106 balls and hit four fours and a six.
Vettori showed a maturity beyond his years with careful defence combined with some bold attacking shots to finish the innings 29 not out.
Tailenders Heath Davis and Geoff Allott were removed by fast-medium Darren Gough.
He bowled Davis with a fast inswinger then, after hitting Allott on the left side of his helmet, had him caught by wicketkeeper Alec Stewart.
Gough ended with three for 42, Tufnell took three for 58 while offspinner Robert Croft finished with two for 48, and fast-medium pair Andrew Caddick and Dominic Croft took one wicket each.
